issues.issue: D ~ N(0,1) is one reading of 'random Gaussian', but it is 112x off the scale the method's own constraint asks for, and that mismatch changes checkpoint selection for the gauss arm only. As written, both the Q2 contrast (gauss vs zero) and the Q3 TFPS arm depend on this audit-chosen scale through a side channel that has nothing to do with routing, and the only protection (pure-val-MSE re-selection) is non-gating.
issues.evidence: Derived from code. (a) layers/Constraint.py: loss_d1 = 1e-3*||diag(D^T D) - I||_F targets unit-norm columns; loss_d2 = 1e-3*||offblock(D^T D)||_F. For a 112x112 D ~ N(0,1): diag(D^T D) ~ 112, so loss_d1 ~ 1e-3*sqrt(112)*111 ~ 1.18; off-block entries have variance 112 over 9408 entries, so loss_d2 ~ 1e-3*sqrt(9408*112) ~ 1.03. Two EDESC instances with alpha=gama=1 add ~4.4 to the training loss and to the validation loss (exp/exp_main.py:130, :257-262), about 10x the forecast MSE (~0.4). For D=0 the same terms are 2*1e-3*sqrt(112) ~ 0.021 and constant; for D ~ N(0, 1/112) they are ~0.02. (b) EarlyStopping (utils/tools.py:40-63) saves on any decrease of that sum. Under N(0,1) the constraint term falls every epoch while Adam shrinks D (roughly lr per entry per step; my estimate at H=192 is ~0.1 per epoch at first, decaying with the type3 0.9^epoch schedule), which is larger than epoch-to-epoch changes in val MSE for many epochs. So tfps_gauss is likely to save late checkpoints chosen by the constraint term, while tfps_zero selects on val MSE plus a constant. (c) At H=192 (lr 5e-4, type3) Adam can move an entry of D by at most about 5e-4 * 65 steps * ~13 effective epochs ~ 0.4 in total, against an init sd of 1: D stays close to its random draw and cannot reach the constrained set. At sd 1/sqrt(112) ~ 0.094 it can. (d) Cluster.py:68: eta*d = 140 is added to ||z D_i||^2. With N(0,1), ||z D_i||^2 ~ ||z||^2 * chi2_28 (mean 28||z||^2), which swamps 140 for any ||z||^2 above ~5, so s varies across experts by roughly +-27% of 1/4. With unit-norm columns ||z D_i||^2 ~ 0.25||z||^2, so 140 dominates unless ||z||^2 is in the hundreds, and s is almost uniform. So N(0,1) is the scale under which the affinity has the most say in routing (in the paper's favour for Q2) and also the scale that distorts the loss and checkpoint selection (against it for Q2 and Q3). (e) layers/InitializeD.py, the initialiser the repo ships and never calls, returns orthonormal columns (left singular vectors), i.e. the unit-norm scale, not sd 1. An author's advocate would say sd 1 is a strawman on (a), (c) and (e); the audit can answer that sd 1 is the literal default and helps routing on (d). Neither side can be settled from the text.
issues.fix: Do not let one scale carry the verdicts. Pick one of these before FREEZE: (1) preferred: add arm tfps_gauss_unit, D ~ N(0, 1/(n*d)) (10 more TFPS runs, roughly +2.5 to 5 CPU-h; a new arm is the owner's call). State Q2 separately for each scale against zero. For Q3 compute the label against each TFPS arm (gauss sd 1, gauss unit, zero); a negative label (VANISHES / REVERSED / SHRINKS) stands only if every TFPS arm gets a label at least that negative, otherwise report 'Q3 DEPENDS ON D INIT' with the per-arm table. (2) If no arm is added: make the pure-val-MSE checkpoint the primary selection for all TFPS arms in Q2 (so the contrast is not checkpoint timing), require Q3 negative labels to hold under both selection rules and against both tfps_gauss and tfps_zero, and put 'D ~ N(0,1), audit's choice' in every label. In both cases log per epoch, for every TFPS run: val MSE, the two cluster losses, the saved-checkpoint epoch, and ||D||_F, so a reader can see what drove selection. If the PDF states a scale, it replaces all of this.

issues.issue: The routing qualifier and the noise-off arm are close to decided by the code, and neither tests the paper's mechanism. They are fair as descriptions of the released router, but the labels can be read as 'pattern routing does not work'.
issues.evidence: Derived. s is row-normalised (Cluster.py:69), so every s_i is in [0,1] and the row sums to 1; the router adds randn*softplus(s) (SparseMoE.py:59), whose sd is at least softplus(0) = 0.69 and is 0.83 at s = 0.25. Whatever D is, the noise is several times the spread of s, so A will sit near 1/n = 0.25 and the 0.30 threshold will very likely fire. Even a one-hot s would give A well below 1 (my rough estimate is around 0.5). For arm 3: experts were trained under near-random assignment and top-1 gate weight is exactly 1, so the experts are close to interchangeable and switching the noise off at eval only should change little. Training with noise off is the arm that would test affinity routing, and it is not in the design (owner decision 2 specifies eval only).
issues.fix: Keep both, but (1) state in section 7 that the qualifier is expected from the code and give the ceiling: A for a one-hot s under this router, computed once in step (c) by simulation of the router alone, plus the mean per-row max-min of s for each arm, so A is read against what is attainable; (2) reword the qualifier to 'ROUTER NOISE EXCEEDS AFFINITY SPREAD (A = …, ceiling = …)'; (3) add to section 9: 'whether training with noise-free affinity routing improves accuracy is not tested; NOISE-OFF labels concern evaluation of a model trained with the released noisy router'.

issues.issue: How D is drawn is ambiguous and may either make the two D matrices identical or break the pairing between arms.
issues.evidence: PREREG section 5 arm 1: 'drawn from torch's global RNG right after torch.manual_seed(seed) inside EDESC construction (both instances)'. If manual_seed(seed) is called inside each EDESC.__init__, the time and frequency D (both 112x112) are the same matrix, and the global stream is reset mid-construction, so layers built after each EDESC (SparseMoE experts, heads; PatchTST_MoE_backbone_cluster_time.py:47-65) repeat or shift their draws. If it is not re-seeded, the gauss arm consumes 2*12544 extra draws, so for a given seed every later weight differs from the zero arm and the gauss-zero contrast includes an unrelated re-draw of the experts and heads.
issues.fix: Draw D from a dedicated torch.Generator (e.g. seed 30000+seed for time, 40000+seed for frequency) and leave the global stream untouched. Then gauss and zero share every other initial weight for a given seed; self-test that all non-D parameters are bitwise equal across the two arms at step 0. Report the paired difference across seeds next to the Welch CI (Welch stays the gating rule unless the statistics lens prefers paired).

summary: Round-1 blockers are fixed in the rules: correct per-horizon config, corrected router premise with a routing measurement, symmetric CI rules with INCONCLUSIVE. The remaining way the answer can be built in is the choice D ~ N(0,1): it puts about 4.4 of constraint loss into the validation criterion for the gauss arm only (zero arm: 0.02), so checkpoint selection differs by arm for reasons unrelated to routing, and Q3 is judged on that arm alone. tfps_zero is a fair 'affinity-blind' control once D is drawn from a separate generator. Labels need the D-init and baseline set in the suffix.
